fields.features_heading: What One Signed Sheet Misses Across a Package
fields.features_subheading: A client on a package returns for several sessions, sometimes for more than one area. The form keeps consent current each visit.
fields.feature_1:
Your medical director's consent wording

Paste in the consent statements and health questions your medical director approved. The form shows them word for word, and the record keeps the text each client signed.
fields.feature_2:
One consent line for each treatment area

The client ticks the areas booked, such as underarms or lower legs, and initials a consent line for each. The provider sees which areas were agreed to before starting.
fields.feature_3:
A short check-in before each session

Ask 3 questions your clinic picks before every return visit, starting with what has changed since the last session. A changed answer tops the record the provider opens.
fields.feature_4:
A session log the provider fills in

After each session, the provider adds the device, the settings your clinic records, and their name. Every session in the package lands on one record, next to the signed consent.
fields.feature_5:
E-signatures on the client's own phone

Send the link with the booking confirmation, or hand over the front desk tablet. The app captures the e-signature and saves it with the answers it confirms, in a database you own.
fields.feature_6:
Full code in your GitHub repository

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository when the form has to live on your clinic's website. Your developer can host it on your own servers and keep building.

Calla sees any change after session 3 first

Odalys Brennan is due for session 4 of her underarm package at Juniper Row Med Spa. The night before, she answers the 3 check-in questions on her phone and marks one change since session 3. Provider Calla Imrie opens the record in the treatment room, and that answer is the first line she reads.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Laser Consent Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a laser hair removal consent form clients sign for each area and check in on before every session.
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every area you treat, such as underarms, lower legs, and the bikini line. Each one becomes a choice on the form with its own consent line, so a client signs only for the areas booked.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask your medical director for the wording of every consent statement and health question. Have a healthcare attorney review it before the form goes live, and keep the approved text exactly as written.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Pick 3 short questions a returning client answers before each session, and have your medical director sign off on them. Keep each one to a yes or no with a box for details.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Agree on what the provider records after each session, such as the device and the settings your clinic tracks. Those fields sit on the same record as the signed consent.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the areas, the wording, the check-in, and the provider log into one prompt. Emergent builds the form and the client database behind it. To add an area later, describe the change in a new prompt.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Set when the link goes out
fields.howto_step_6_des: Send the form link with every booking confirmation. Then choose when a client who still has not signed gets it again by email, and whether the front desk hears about it too.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Book a test client for two sessions and add a second area before the second one. Check that the new area asks for its own signature and that both sessions land on one record.

faq_plan.q: What is a laser hair removal consent form?
faq_plan.a: A laser hair removal consent form is the record that a client agreed to laser hair removal on named areas. It holds the consent statements from your medical director, the client's answers to your health questions, and the signature and date.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a laser hair removal consent form?
faq_plan.a: Gather your treatment areas, the consent wording your medical director signed off on, and the check-in questions for return visits. Describe all of it in plain English to Emergent's AI form builder. Emergent builds a working form and a table of client records from that one prompt, and you prompt again to add an area later.

faq_plan.q: How do I adapt a laser hair removal consent form template to my clinic?
faq_plan.ref: laser hair removal consent form template
faq_plan.secondary: laser hair removal consent form template
faq_plan.a: Replace the template's wording first, because a laser hair removal consent form template was written for another clinic and your medical director's text belongs in its place. Then cut the areas you do not treat, add your own health questions, and give return visits a short check-in.

faq_plan.q: Can a laser hair removal consent form also cover laser tattoo removal?
faq_plan.a: It can share the client record, but not the consent wording. Ask your medical director for separate wording for tattoo removal, with its own section and signature. Each record then shows which treatment the client agreed to. A tattoo consent form is a different document again, for getting a tattoo rather than removing one.

faq_plan.q: How should a laser hair removal consent form handle a package of sessions?
faq_plan.a: Have the client sign the full consent before the first session. Before each later session, the client answers a few check-in questions instead of signing everything again. Log every session on the same record with its date and provider, and the package shows sessions used and sessions left. Ask your medical director when a full signature is due again.

faq_plan.q: Can a laser hair removal consent form cover intense pulsed light treatments too?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if your medical director writes wording for each. Give intense pulsed light its own section with its own consent statements, and let the booked treatment decide which section the client sees. The provider log then names the device used at each session.

faq_plan.q: Should a laser hair removal consent form record the provider for each session?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Record the provider who performs each session, along with the date. When a package is shared between providers, the record then shows who did each one. Log the artist the same way on a permanent makeup consent form, where touch-ups follow the first visit.

faq_plan.q: Can clients sign a laser hair removal consent form on their phone before the visit?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A phone link replaces the printed laser hair removal consent form PDF that clients fill in at the front desk. The client signs on their own phone from the booking email. An app built with Emergent can capture the e-signature, and every signed form lives in a database you own. Ask your healthcare attorney what your clinic needs for consent signed electronically.

faq_plan.q: Is there a free laser hair removal consent form I can use?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing. Your consent form has no response caps, however many clients sign it across every package.

faq_plan.q: Can a laser hair removal consent form share a client record with a waxing consent?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Give each service its own consent form and signature, and save both to the same client record. A client booked for laser on the legs and a brow wax then has two signed forms in one place, each dated. Write the waxing consent form with its own questions rather than reusing the laser wording.

plan.angle: The top 10 is clinic PDFs, a Pinterest pin, Scribd copies and a template listing: one static sheet signed once. Laser hair removal is sold as a series of sessions across several body areas, so this page shows what a single sheet cannot: a consent line per treatment area, a short check-in before each session, a provider log on the same record, and a package that follows the client between locations. Clinical content stays with the clinic: the page never states risks, results, skin suitability or who may operate a laser, and leaves the wording to the medical director.
